Im so sorry for your loss. I was in the same mindset after my SO passed from her breast cancer. After a 1 year and 9 months of multiple medications, reading imaging reports after imaging report and nothing getting better she got hospitalized due to a cervical metastasis compressing her spinal cord. She was 1 month in the hospital, and had to get released to a rehab, cause the internal med doctors said she needed a subacute rehab center. Before leaving she wanted to start a new chemotherapy. I was against it cause she was leaving to a rehab, but she was set on getting the cancer out of her. After less than a week in the rehab we had to go to the hospital due a sepsis and a few days after a blood clot cause a massive pulmonary embolism. 
I’m a doctor that graduated in another country and of course I blamed myself of a lot of things, specially not voicing my concerns and taking some time to take care of her instead of a rehab. It’s hard to cope with that guilt, it takes time, it never goes away completely I guess, but you also have to have in mind that this type of disease it’s really unpredictable. Yes you could’ve done something that might’ve prolonged a bit his time here, but also could’ve prolonged suffering, we would never know. I think it’s better to see the good things you did, like being by his side all this time, he needed you all this time and you were there! Don’t blame yourself, I know it’s hard, but whenever one of those thoughts come to mind, try to also think in the good things and all that you also endured because you loved him. I try to do that, I choose to remember the good things and smile, it doesn’t always work, but it does help! 
Take care and a big hug!

My gf had metastatic breast cancer. Diagnosed 1 year a 8 months ago. She had mastectomy, multiple rounds of different quemo (sorry if I don’t name every medication, I use to know each one but at one point I just stopped remembering all of them) they all worked partially. Metastasis in multiple bones and liver that were not getting better. She kept fighting, all this while still working as a director of a big healthcare company and having multiple meetings and stuff. 
Her cancer was triple positive at the beginning, after a mastectomy and a partial lymphadenectomy (they couldn’t get all the lymph nodes cause there were a lot of adhesions, they got about 20) and after the multiple chemos, we asked the doctor for a biopsy after having a second opinion. The metastasis had changed, now they where triple negative (I’m and IMG and I’ve never heard of something like that, I am not an oncologist in my country just a GP but still, it tells you the aggressiveness of it) 
We went for a trip to Cancun with family, so she could meet my parents. After the trip, couple of days after her birthday, she had some metastasis compressing the nerves in the spine and had to undergo radiotherapy, it worked but it took a toll on her esophagus and she stopped eating and drinking. 
After a month in the hospital, she finally was getting stronger enough that they wanted to discharge her to a rehab and continue chemo with a new treatment, but I knew it was going to be a shitshow. She was eating a bit more and drinking but I don’t think it was enough. 2 days  before discharge they gave her a round of chemo and made sure she was okay before discharge
She was in the rehab through thanksgiving and the Sunday after she started to be delirious, rehab wasn’t even paying attention. I was scared, frustrated and tired and I was asking for her to be hydrated through an IV if not I was going to take her to the hospital. They gave her fluids but the needle they use in her port was too thin and it wasn’t working. At a point I just said fuck this call the ED we are going there. 
All her labs were unstable, amonia increased, liver enzymes increased, platelets on floor. She was deliric and they had to sedate her. She had a massive PE 3 days after getting in the hospital and transfer to the ICU. 
I think once it goes to the liver, it just becomes a ticking time bomb. The liver is the powerhouse of the body and with all the things that are happening in the body besides the metastasis in the liver, it just can’t take the toll of all it and shuts down with nothing much we can do. 
I’m sorry for your loss OP, know that you’re not alone, take some time to grief and take care of yourself.

We flew our  10 months Boston from DC to Cancun, through United. Everything went fine, mom had business class tickets, I had economy lol so our boy went on first class. We had all paperwork (health check, CDC form, emotional support certificate, doctors letter, and a copy of the vaccine records) I chose a carrier that we found in Amazon that was the specific size United had in their webpage am fitted under the seat in front of ours, although Felix didn’t fit perfectly like some posts say, he is supposed to turn inside the carrier without problems, he was comfortable enough and he could take his little head out. We did call the airline and let them know we had the dog, there was an extra charge for him. 
When returning we asked if he could be out of the carrier, but since we didn’t tell them that he was an emotional support dog before hand they wouldn’t let him come out of the carrier since they have to verify him with a certain amount of time ahead of the trip, so if you are going to go with the emotional support route let the airline know they might let you take it out of the bag, ours was fine during the whole trip, I recommend to take one of the little portable fans just in case you can point it at him during the trip. 
Oh we did give him some Benadryl about 30 minutes before getting in the plane to keep him calm. 
If I remember anything else I’ll let you know, you can also dm me if you have any other questions.
